name: 510 Visuals
summary: A website for a studio that builds giant LED and media installations, designed to feel as engineered as the work itself.
objective-cadet: 5 TEN designs and builds huge light-up installations: LED ceilings, media walls, the New Year's Eve ball. The site was planned, mocked up and designed from the ground up to show the scale of their work and where it lives around the world, and to feel as precise as their engineering.
objective-engineer: Built from the ground up: planned and mocked up first, designed in Figma, then built in Webflow with Client-First structure, a Three.js globe fed by the Projects collection, GSAP scroll systems and Unicorn Studio WebGL, all editable by the team in the CMS.
params:
Their project work has to lead, not the agency copy
Every project pinned to where it was installed
The client edits content in the Webflow Editor
Heavy 3D can't tank mobile performance
manifest-pages: Homepage, About, Projects, Project template, Inspiration, BNY Space, Services, Contact
handoff: Client-First classes, an editor-ready CMS and every script on GitHub behind an init guard.
quote: [Testimonial from 5 TEN. Placeholder until the quote comes in.]

name: Daniel Aguirre Law
client: Law Firm of Daniel Aguirre · Wallingford, CT
summary: A bilingual immigration-law site that proves a nationwide record with a live case-results map, wrapped in a warm cream-glass design.
objective-cadet: An immigration firm in Connecticut serves families in 14+ states, in English and Spanish. Most law-firm sites feel cold and generic. This one had to feel warm and trustworthy, and prove the firm's reach at a glance.
objective-engineer: Designed and built from the ground up: planned and mocked up first, designed in Figma, then built custom in Webflow on Client-First, with a D3 case-results map as the hero, a cream-glass design language, a two-tier navigation, and a connected content system (vocabulary, insights, practice areas) that the firm edits in the CMS.
params:
Everything works in English and Spanish
Case results come from the CMS, never hard-coded
Warm and human, not "stock law firm"
The firm updates content without a developer
manifest-pages: Homepage, About, Expertise, Practice area template, Immigration hub, Humanitarian hub, Case results, Reviews, Insights, Contact
manifest-collections: Case Results, Practice Areas, Insights, Topics
handoff: Cream-glass components, a bilingual content model and versioned stylesheets the firm never has to touch.
quote: [Testimonial from the Law Firm of Daniel Aguirre. Placeholder until the quote comes in.]

name: AB Identity
summary: The identity for this portfolio: an orbit mark, a square-first system and one hot accent in deep space.
objective-cadet: A portfolio for someone who builds interactive websites needed its own look: confident, a little playful, and clearly "space". Everything had to work as a tiny icon and as a giant headline.
objective-engineer: A mark built on a golden-ratio grid, a token set (void, deep, panel, starlight, signal), square components with zero radius, and type roles for display, body and mono, all mapped to CMS-editable variables.
params:
Readable at 16px (favicon) and at 200px
One accent color, used sparingly
Square corners everywhere
Works on dark and light sections
manifest-pages: Orbit mark, Construction grid, Light + dark lockups, Color tokens, Type roles, Favicon, Avatar, Cards + stickers
handoff: One Figma library and matching Webflow variables, so every new page starts on-brand.
